subject: Proposal: staged patch sequencing, version pin cohesion, and stepback window
messages:
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>, Riverton Health <engops@rivertonhealth.com>
Cc: DocSec Integrations <integrations@docsign.com>
Date: Tue, 9 May 2028 09:02:00 -0000
Subject: Proposal: staged patch sequencing, version pin cohesion, and stepback window

Team / Riverton ops,

Following our call last week, I'm proposing a coordinated approach for the upcoming private deployment maintenance so we can minimize customer impact while preserving the ability to step back quickly if we notice regressions. High level: a phased patch sequence, an explicit version-cohesion rule set for pinned customers, and a 2-hour stepback window during the first tranche.

Key asks:
- Riverton: confirm preferred weekly maintenance windows (we have Tue/Wed 02:00-06:00 UTC as options).
- Karthik & Markus: review the patch sequencing in the attached patch_matrix_v1.xlsx and call out any cross-service dependency ordering constraints.
- Stephanie: draft a short customer comms version and a runbook checklist that can be used by on-call.

Proposed sequencing (short):
1) Control plane (canary hosts) - patch minimal controlplane nodes and run smoke checks (~15m).
2) KV-cache nodes - minor rolling restart, validate cache warmup metrics.
3) Model-serving agents (staged by shard) - small canary -> 10% -> 50% -> remaining.
4) Network and infra packages - if changes require kernel updates, reserve separate window.

Version cohesion: for pinned customers we will not move major runtime version in the same tranche; pin groups must either be fully moved together or left untouched. We propose a "soft lock" period of 48 hours after the patch for evaluation before wider unpinning.

Stepback window: for tranche 1 we will keep a 2-hour stepback where we can re-pin traffic to the previous runtime and roll back the canary models. This requires pre-captured snapshots of key artifacts and KMS access verification.

Attachments: patch_matrix_v1.xlsx (spreadsheet with candidate sequence, estimated durations), maintenance_comms_draft.md

Please review and reply with signoffs or redlines by EOD so we can firm the schedule with Riverton.

Thanks,
Naomi
Naomi Feldman
Head of Customer Operations, Redwood Inference
naomi.feldman@redwood.com

Subject: Re: Proposal: staged patch sequencing, version pin cohesion, and stepback window

Naomi — thanks for the clear plan. A few technical notes after scanning patch_matrix_v1.xlsx:

- Control plane canary: we need an extra preflight for the orchestration layer config where a node-level change can lead to scheduling anomalies. Add a 10-minute drift-validation that runs twice before promoting.
- KV-cache node restarts must maintain pinned-tenant read affinity. For Riverton (pinned group: tenant-riverton-a), we need to ensure an explicit TTL warmup and not evict their prefixes during the window.
- Model-serving agents: propose we do canary per availability zone, not per shard. Network latencies across AZs can hide regressions.
- Kernel updates: mark as "hard dependency" and schedule into a separate safety window. If kernel changes are required, the stepback becomes impossible without node reprovisioning.

I flagged three sequence rows in the spreadsheet (rows 12, 18, 23) with dependency notes. Also added a column called 'stepback-ready' — will fill that out by 17:00.

One ask for Riverton: can you confirm whether you will allow a short read-only redirect for up to 30 minutes if we detect KV degradation? That helps avoid full rollback.

-Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Senior Engineering Manager, Serving Runtime

Hi Naomi / Karthik,

Thanks — Riverton can support a Tue maintenance window starting 02:00 UTC. A few constraints from our side:
- No more than two kernel-level changes in the same week; any kernel change must be approved 72 hours prior.
- We can accept a 30-minute read-only redirect as an intermediate mitigation, but we need a documented test plan for that behavior.
- For pinned tenants we require an explicit rollback checklist that includes replayable audit logs and a snapshot of model artifacts.

We reviewed the spreadsheet and the 'stepback-ready' flag is helpful. If Karthik can mark which rows are "stepback-immediate" vs "stepback-reprovision", that will let our infra lead plan staffing.

Confirming: Tue 02:00-06:00 UTC is acceptable for tranche 1 canary, pending your final signoff on the control-plane preflight.

Thanks,
Ellen Park
Senior EngOps Manager, Riverton Health
engops@rivertonhealth.com

Thanks Ellen — Tuesday 02:00-06:00 UTC works; we will treat kernel updates as a separate approval flow.

Quick summary / agreed actions:
- Karthik: finalize 'stepback-ready' and label rows as 'immediate' vs 'reprovision' by 17:00 today. (Action: fill spreadsheet column)
- Stephanie: publish customer-facing maintenance note from maintenance_comms_draft.md, include explicit read-only redirect behavior and the audit-log snapshot steps. (Action: publish + send 48h notice)
- Riverton (Ellen): confirm staffing for Tue 02:00-06:00 UTC and that your infra lead can review Karthik's final labels by 18:00. (Action: confirm)
- Naomi: I'll schedule the maintenance bridge and ensure DocSec has the access tokens for the artifact snapshots; will send DocuSign link for the updated mutual action plan after signoff.

If anything changes, flag immediately in this thread — otherwise I'll mark "provisionally scheduled" and create a JIRA-OPS-9821 runbook with the stepback checklist.

Best,
Naomi
